title: Exposure at work, illness and income
why_feedback: Exposure harms health, illness costs earnings, and lost earnings may leave workers with fewer choices to avoid exposed work.
contexts: Outdoor informal work in Delhi and other Indian cities
caveats: The first link has mixed evidence; the two return links have not been measured. Treat as a plausible loop to test, not a finding.

title: Clean fuel costs and household smoke
why_feedback: When refills are unaffordable, households burn solid fuels, smoke harms health, medical bills rise, and less money is left for clean fuel.
contexts: Low-income households with gas connections in India
caveats: The affordability and smoke links are well evidenced; the health and spending links are mixed, the return link is unmeasured, and the HAPIN trial found limited health gains from partial exposure reduction.

title: Monitoring gaps that hide exposure
why_feedback: Places without monitors have unrecorded exposure, unrecorded exposure is less likely to be prioritised, and unprioritised places may not get monitors.
contexts: Rural and small-town India, especially Bihar and Uttar Pradesh
caveats: An institutional interpretation built on a measured mismatch between monitor placement and pollution. Not studied end to end.

title: Kiln enforcement and transition costs
why_feedback: Polluting kilns face orders; orders require investment; cost and skills constraints slow conversion, so polluting kilns continue.
contexts: Brick kilns in Bihar and Bangladesh
caveats: Evidence on the return link is contradictory: Bihar reports most kilns converted after a mandate. The loop may weaken where mandates are paired with finance and training.

title: A regional problem met by local action
why_feedback: Pollution crosses borders, so city action alone is limited; uncoordinated upwind burning continues; smoke crosses borders again.
caveats: The coordination-to-burning link is unmeasured, and Punjab's recent fall in fires shows state action can weaken the loop.

title: Emergency rules and compliance
why_feedback: Bans that cause uncompensated hardship may weaken compliance, letting dust continue and keeping episodes severe.
caveats: Two of four links are interpretations only. Included so readers can see where research would change the picture.
